paragraphs.source_en: The affair left not only Ieyasu's retainers marveling, but Hasegawa Hidekazu and Chaya Shirōjirō utterly dumbfounded. Once they reached Yamaguchi Tōzaemon Mitsuhiro at Tawara, Hidekazu and Shirōjirō would be on familiar ground for the remainder of the journey. Naturally, what impressed those two was quite different from what had impressed Kanbara Koheita.

paragraphs.source_en: “That was truly great compassion from the depths of his heart.” So Shirōjirō marveled, while Hasegawa said with boundless admiration, “His wit and strategy are in no way inferior to those of the late Minister of the Right.”

paragraphs.source_en: Word that Ieyasu had persuaded a maddened peasant army on the road had long since reached Mitsutoshi and his son. But the father and son were startled.

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu's party remained in Tawara for less than an hour. During that time, Mitsutoshi's son, Kyūemon Mitsumoto, assumed they would stay the night and hurried about with Hasegawa Hidekazu recruiting warriors to accompany them.
